title: REE Literature Evidence v1
description: A single literature entry's record.json. `additionalProperties` is false at the top level, and stays false on purpose: this object is a record of the corpus's actual convention, not a free-form bag. Reconciled against full-corpus usage twice on 2026-08-14 -- first the `source` object, then everything outside it -- using `scripts/audit_literature_schema.py --drift`, which reports for each undeclared key how many records use it, in how many literature_type directories, over what date range. That enumeration is what decides direction, and it should be re-run rather than reasoned from a sample. Corpus-wide and still-current usage is convention: widen the schema (that is how `source.pmid` and `evidence_direction_per_claim` got in). Usage confined to ONE directory from ONE pull session on ONE date is drift: normalise the records instead. Three kinds of content were rejected on that basis and belong elsewhere: (a) per-entry annotation labels from a single pull -- put them in `tags`, where the `prefix:value` form is already an established idiom; (b) prose -- provenance notes, metadata corrections, retrieval caveats, retagging rationale -- which belongs in the entry's summary.md, the dominant corpus convention; and (c) bespoke `confidence_components` names, against which the canonical three are used exactly by 2132 of the 2143 records that carry the object. ENFORCED SINCE 2026-08-14 by `scripts/validate_literature.py`, wired into the PreToolUse `git commit` guard via `scripts/precommit_literature.sh` (install with `REE_Working/scripts/install_literature_commit_gate.py`). Before that date nothing read this schema at all -- no hook, no CI job, no indexer check -- which is why the `source` drift above accumulated for six months unseen. The gate is REPORT-ONLY until the corpus baseline reaches zero (17 findings in 17 of 2189 records at the time it landed): it is scoped to the records a commit touches, so turning on REE_LITERATURE_GATE_BLOCK=1 will not wedge unrelated commits. The validator also checks what a JSON Schema cannot -- that a record is REACHABLE by build_experiment_indexes._scan_literature's glob at all, that literature_type/entry_id agree with their directories, and that summary_path resolves on disk.

source.description: Bibliographic provenance for the cited work. Declares three groups: descriptive fields (title/authors/year/venue), stable external identifiers (doi/pmid/pmc/pmcid/arxiv_id/isbn/url), and in-publication locators (volume/issue/pages). `additionalProperties` stays false on purpose, so this object is a record of the corpus's actual citation convention rather than a free-form bag. Two things deliberately do NOT belong here and are rejected: (a) denormalised renderings of fields already declared separately (a formatted `citation` string, a merged `volume_pages`), and (b) prose -- provenance notes, metadata corrections, retrieval caveats -- which belong in the entry's summary.md, the dominant corpus convention. An optional identifier may be null, meaning 'checked, none exists', which is more informative than omitting the key.

pmid.description: PubMed ID, digits only. The primary verification handle for a biomedical source and the most-used identifier in this corpus after doi.

pmc.description: PubMed Central ID, 'PMC'-prefixed. Synonym of `pmcid`; both are declared because both are already in use with identical value format. New entries should prefer `pmc`.

pmcid.description: Deprecated spelling of `pmc`. Retained so existing entries validate; do not use in new entries.

isbn.description: ISBN for a book-form source, where no doi exists.

url.description: Canonical link, for a source with no doi or other stable identifier.

volume.description: Journal volume. String or integer -- both spellings are already in use.

issue.description: Journal issue. String or integer -- both spellings are already in use.

evidence_direction.description: Direction of this source's bearing on the claims in `claim_ids_tested`. The enum is closed and matches the tokens `build_experiment_indexes._normalize_direction` actually honours -- widening it here WITHOUT widening that function produces a record that validates but is silently ingested as 'unknown', which is worse than a rejected record. A 2026-08-14 entry carrying the non-enum token 'refines' was in exactly that state and was corrected to 'mixed' rather than admitted.

evidence_direction_per_claim.description: Per-claim direction overrides, e.g. {"MECH-303": "supports", "MECH-304": "weakens"}. Without it, an entry testing several claims applies one blanket `evidence_direction` to all of them. This is the SAME convention already mandated for experiment manifests with more than one claim (umbrella CLAUDE.md; read by serve.py and by the indexer's experiment path), so the literature entries using it are early adopters of an existing cross-corpus convention rather than local drift -- which is why this field is admitted where the rest of the 2026-08-14 top-level drift was normalised away instead. A claim absent here falls back to `evidence_direction`.
